title: Per-message deadline shaping and cooperative cancellation adapter for Go SDK streaming
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: consumers of the Go SDK stream API often need per-message time budgets that differ from the overall request deadline (e.g., synthesize a 60s overall stream with 150ms per-message latency SLOs). Current SDK exposes only the upstream context deadline which makes it hard to enforce per-frame budgets, produce consistent metrics, and implement graceful abort/retry policies.

This ticket implements a cooperative cancellation adapter and per-message deadline-shaping layer in the Go SDK streaming stack. Goals: expose a simple pattern for callers, ensure deadlines are honored end-to-end (client + wire + server), emit clear metrics for cancellation reasons, and provide fallback strategies (short-circuit to non-streaming or allow last-chunk drain) when per-message budgets are exhausted.

Key deliverables: adapter in sdk/stream/adapter.go, demo examples in examples/streaming_deadline_shaping/, unit and integration tests, a small migration note for existing users, and a short Console dashboard panel for per-message cancel reasons (instrumentation hooks).
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes NewPerMessageAdapter(parentCtx, options) that returns a child context manager and helper to compute per-message deadlines
Adapter enforces per-message deadlines without cancelling the entire stream immediately (supports graceful drain window configurable, default 200ms)
Metrics emitted: stream.per_message_latency, stream.cancel_reason (values: deadline_exceeded, parent_cancel, user_abort, network_error)
Integration tests that simulate slow server responses causing per-message deadline cancellations and asserting adapter behavior
A documented example (Go) showing common patterns: short-lived interactive messages, batch streams with long parent deadline, and an autoscaling knob example for Dedicated
implementation_notes:
Design notes: we will implement a light-weight coordinator that: (1) derives per-message deadlines from a provided policy (fixed budget, percent of remaining parent time, or explicit per-message values), (2) wraps the send/receive per-message operations with a nested context that is cancelled on per-message timeout but does not necessarily cancel the parent stream context, (3) supports a graceful drain period where the current in-flight message is allowed to finish if it crosses the per-message budget but not the drain window, and (4) exposes hooks to mark a message as retriable vs terminal.

Trade-offs: doing aggressive per-message cancellation reduces tail latency but can increase upstream load (more retries). We provide an options flag to automatically switch to a non-streaming fallback if cancel rate exceeds threshold.

API sketch: NewPerMessageAdapter(parentCtx, PerMessageOptions{BudgetMS:150, DrainMS:200, Policy:"fixed"}) -> {NextMessageCtx(messageMeta) context.Context, MarkRetriable(), MarkCompleted()}.

Testing plan: unit tests for deadline math, race-detector runs for concurrent streams, integration test against a test server that delays frames with controllable jitter, and a manual perf run on Dedicated small GPU to measure overhead.

Observability: emit tags: model, route, client_version, message_index. Wire up to Console events and add a short dashboard panel for top cancel reasons and retry amplification rate.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Maya Thompson: Initial design doc uploaded to Drive: https://drive.internal.redwood/designs/go-sdk/per-message-adapter. Marked P1 due to several customer reports about inconsistent streaming latency.

2025-02-18 - Ravi Patel: Spike complete. Prototype adapter implemented in local branch feature/ENG-142857-permessage-adapter. Found a race when parent context cancels while per-message timer is active; added a cancellation handshake to avoid double-cancel semantics.

2025-02-20 - Ana-Maria Ruiz (reviewer): Suggest exposing a percent-of-parent policy in addition to fixed budget. Also recommended emitting a histogram of 'message_time_budget_usage' to help tuning. Leaving as action items.

2025-02-25 - Ravi Patel: Addressed review comments. Added percent policy and histogram metrics. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/942. Tests added: TestPerMessageDeadline_ShapesBudget, TestDrainWindow_AllowsLateFinish.

2025-03-01 - Infrastructure: Ran integration tests against dedicated-ci (small worker) to validate timing semantics. Observed a 0.8% CPU overhead for adapter on busy loop workloads. Decided this is acceptable; flagged for perf docs.

2025-03-05 - QA: Flaky test observed in TestPerMessageDeadline_RetryAmplification when simulated network jitter > 500ms. Root cause: our default retry backoff allowed immediate retries. Proposed change: add jittered backoff in adapter MarkRetriable path.
notes: Follow-up: consider a language-idiomatic helper for TypeScript/Python SDKs once Go API stabilizes
Coordinate with runtime team to ensure server signals (e.g., truncated frames) map to cancel_reason=network_error when appropriate
Document migration steps: default behavior preserved; opt-in via NewPerMessageAdapter call
